raw_response:
I am not going to spread all 9 mu into one crop. Cotton is still my main crop because I have planted it many years and I know how to manage it, but cotton takes more labor and money, and the price is never fully certain. So I will keep most land in cotton, then leave some land for maize and mungbean. Maize gives steadier grain, and mungbean does not need so much fertilizer, so if the year is not smooth I still have something to fall back on. I only finished primary school, so I do not calculate too finely. I mostly look at what worked on my own land and what nearby farmers are doing. Last years, if I cut fertilizer too much, the crop looked weak, so this year I will not save too hard on that. But my family also has people working off-farm, so I cannot choose a plan that needs too much hand labor everywhere.

For cotton, I will do the biggest area and manage it carefully with base fertilizer plus one topdressing, and irrigate when it is dry because I have well water. For maize, I will keep input moderate, not too fancy, just enough to make sure it does not go yellow in the fast growing stage. For mungbean, I will keep it simple and low-cost. That crop is mainly for spreading risk and bringing some cash without too much spending. I still watch every yuan, so I will use improved seed where it matters, but not chase the most expensive inputs.
